clue.text: Police district of American composer

parts.note: a cop is a police officer, standing for the police
land can mean a region or district

explanation.surface: A question about which police precinct an American composer belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron Copland was a twentieth-century composer from the United States, known for Appalachian Spring.

clue.text: May one? Never in Greece!

definitions.meaning: the first day of a Roman month was its ..., so the first of May is one
'at the Greek ...' means never, as the Greeks had no such day

explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like a verb asking permission; it is the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Calends are the first day of a Roman month, and the Greek calends is a proverbial time that never comes.

clue.text: Having a share of suffering in some areas, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken and heard as a similar-sounding word

parts.note: a body hurting in places is 'part aching'

explanation.surface: Wondering whether sharing in something means suffering in places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part aching' (suffering in some areas) said aloud sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To partake of something is to take a share or portion of it.

clue.text: A line frequently up in the rigging

parts.note: oft is an old word for often, frequently

explanation.surface: A sailor's rope often seen high among a ship's ropes and spars.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloft is the nautical word for high up among the masts and sails.

clue.text: What is the harm in putting locking mechanism around border?

indicators.note: around says the mechanism's word wraps about the word for border

parts.note: a detent is a catch or pawl that locks a moving part
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Asking what damage could come from fitting a lock round an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Detriment is damage or loss suffered by someone or something.

clue.text: Crave cheese-spread on crust of bread

indicators.note: the crust is the outside, here the first letter of the word bread
spread means the letters of cheese are spread about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Longing for cheese spread on a crust of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheese-spread' reads as a single food; split it, and 'spread' is the signal to rearrange CHEESE.
explanation.definitionFit: To beseech is to beg earnestly, to crave as a favour.

clue.text: Living creature

definitions.meaning: a living thing, as in a human or alien one

explanation.definitionFit: Being means existing, and a being is a creature, as in a human or alien one.

clue.text: Stories involving additional Amerind chiefs

indicators.note: involving means one word takes in the other

parts.note: sagas are long stories
more means extra, additional

explanation.surface: Tales that bring in still more Native American leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: A sagamore was a subordinate chief among the Algonquian peoples of North America.

clue.text: Gantry displaying hotel merchandise, in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A gantry at a hotel showing off goods for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinclair Lewis's novel is Elmer Gantry, so the definition asks for the first name that goes with, or is shown alongside, Gantry.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmer is the first name of Gantry, the preacher in Sinclair Lewis's novel of that title.

clue.text: Yokel and top tennis player supporting country dance

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits below the one it holds up

parts.note: the hay is an old English country dance
a seed is a top-ranked player in a tennis draw

explanation.surface: A rustic and a leading tennis star propping up a folk dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A hayseed is an unsophisticated country person, a bumpkin.

clue.text: Slow passage of long, old ship

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek legend

explanation.surface: A leisurely voyage aboard an ancient vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, a largo is a movement or section played very slowly and broadly.

clue.text: Emaciated and toothless, what's-his-name?

parts.note: emaciated means very thin
having no teeth leaves only gums, so gummy

explanation.surface: Trying to recall the name of a gaunt, toothless man.
explanation.definitionFit: A word used for a person or thing whose name is forgotten, like whatsit.

clue.text: Narrow escape when negative terminal is running to ground

indicators.note: a terminal is an end, here the front end of the word negative

parts.note: earthing is connecting a circuit to the ground

explanation.surface: An electrical scare where the negative terminal is wired to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terminal' can be either end of a word; here it is the first, N. Earthing is British for what Americans call grounding a circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A near thing is a close shave, a situation that almost ended badly.

clue.text: Scrap of food left out for a walrus

indicators.note: out says a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a morsel is a small piece of food

explanation.surface: A bit of food set aside for a walrus to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse is an old name for the walrus, from a Lapp or Russian word.

clue.text: Sun, type of big star

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday, or sun
pica is a size of printing type

explanation.surface: The sun described as a kind of giant star.
explanation.definitionFit: Spica is the brightest star in the constellation Virgo, a blue giant.

clue.text: What tourists in Greece may see, a harvest on poor soil

definitions.text: What tourists in Greece may see

parts.note: a crop is what is harvested

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters of soil are in bad shape, rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek sightseer's view of a meagre harvest from bad land.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of SOIL gives OLIS to end the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acropolis of Athens, crowned by the Parthenon, is Greece's best-known sight for visitors.

clue.text: Bedeck with flowers, a king in this blessed plot

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

parts.note: John of Gaunt calls his country 'this blessed plot' in Shakespeare's Richard II
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: Decorating with garlands, a monarch in his beloved land.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation 'This blessed plot, this earth, this realm, this England' is from Shakespeare's Richard II.
explanation.definitionFit: To engarland is to put a garland on, to festoon with flowers.

clue.text: Judo exponent in pleasant suburban area

definitions.meaning: a judoka holding the green grade of belt
the protected open countryside around a town

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the green belt is a planning designation keeping open land around towns from development.
explanation.definitionFit: A green belt is a judo grade and its wearer, and also the protected undeveloped land ringing a British city.

clue.text: Nice papal turn-out, in a fire engine!

indicators.note: a turn-out of letters is a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: A pope's visit to Nice prompts a crowd, with a fire engine attending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn-out' reads as a crowd at a papal visit, and also as the callout of a fire crew; in the wordplay it rearranges NICE PAPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Fire services call their vehicles appliances, a pump being an appliance.

clue.text: Smoke from grate etc, I disperse

indicators.note: to disperse is to scatter, so the letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: Smoke coming from a fireplace and the rest, which I spread around.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoke is a colloquial name for a cigarette.

clue.text: Medical treatment demanded

indicators.note: treatment of the letters means they are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Medical care being insisted upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Claimed means asserted a right to, demanded as due.

clue.text: Mince-pies, a brown colour

indicators.note: to mince is to chop small, so the letters are chopped and rearranged

explanation.surface: Mince pies having a brownish shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince-pies' reads as the Christmas pastry; 'Mince' is the anagram signal for PIES A.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown pigment, originally made from cuttlefish ink.

clue.text: Gateway to hell found in cavern usually

indicators.note: found in means the answer is sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: The entrance to the underworld generally lies in a cave.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Avernus near Naples was held by the Romans to be the entrance to the underworld.

clue.text: Like an anchor in a voyage

parts.note: a trip is a journey or voyage

explanation.surface: An anchor carried along on a sea journey.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is atrip when it has just been lifted clear of the seabed.

clue.text: Colophony as an aid to bowing

definitions.meaning: the amber resin left after distilling turpentine
string players rub it on the bow hair for grip

explanation.definitionFit: Rosin is the resin also called colophony, rubbed on violin bows to make them grip the strings.

clue.text: Wife-batterer calling with point of story

parts.note: Mr Punch beats his wife Judy in the Punch and Judy puppet show
a line is a line of work, a calling

explanation.surface: A violent husband and his job alongside the climax of a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch and Judy is a traditional British seaside puppet show in which Punch hits his wife Judy.
explanation.definitionFit: The punchline is the final phrase that makes a joke or story land.

clue.text: Quiet English painter, trifling

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
William Etty was an English painter of nudes

explanation.surface: A quiet English artist of little importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty means small and unimportant, trivial.

clue.text: Hospital examination, hourly

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A hospital check carried out every hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Horal is a rare adjective relating to hours, from the Latin hora.

clue.text: Smackers, we hear, beneath this most elite variety of decoration

indicators.note: a variety of letters suggests a different arrangement of them

explanation.surface: Kisses beneath a sprig of the choicest Christmas greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smackers, we hear, beneath this' is an extra hint: smackers are kisses, and people kiss under the sprig at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig of the parasitic evergreen is hung up as a Christmas decoration.

clue.text: Arrest ladder in stocking, at home

parts.note: a ladder in tights or stockings is called a run
in means at home

explanation.surface: A snag in hosiery spotted indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladder' is British for a run in tights; 'run in' is slang for arresting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone in is to take them into police custody.

clue.text: Extremes of disharmony, unpleasant in family

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: nasty means unpleasant

explanation.surface: Discord and unpleasantness within a household.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynasty is a line of rulers or powerful people from one family.

clue.text: But do they prepare bank statements?

definitions.text: But do they prepare bank statements?

parts.words: But do they prepare bank statements?
parts.note: bank clerks who count money, and people who tell things, so they might be expected to issue statements

explanation.definitionFit: Tellers are bank cashiers, and also those who tell or state things.
